trends.note: Reported cases represent only a fraction of estimated cases. Major resurgence observed from 2021 onward, driven by conflicts, climate shocks and COVID-19 health system disruption.

riskFactors.title: Unsafe Water & Inadequate Sanitation
riskFactors.description: Cholera spreads through contaminated water and food. 2.2 billion people globally lack access to safely managed drinking water, creating conditions for endemic transmission.

riskFactors.title: Conflict & Displacement
riskFactors.description: Conflict zones destroy water infrastructure and displace populations into crowded settings with no sanitation. Yemen, Syria, Haiti and Sudan are among the most severely affected.

riskFactors.title: Flooding & Climate Events
riskFactors.description: Floods contaminate water supplies and overwhelm sanitation systems, triggering outbreaks. Climate change is increasing the frequency and severity of flooding globally.

riskFactors.title: Malnutrition
riskFactors.description: Malnourished individuals — especially children — are at significantly higher risk of severe cholera and death due to impaired immune function.

riskFactors.title: Weak Health Systems
riskFactors.description: Countries with limited health infrastructure cannot rapidly detect, report, or respond to cholera outbreaks, allowing them to spread before control measures are implemented.

didYouKnow: Cholera kills within hours if left untreated — but oral rehydration salts (ORS) cost less than $0.50 and are over 90% effective at preventing death.
The current seventh pandemic of cholera has been ongoing since 1961, caused by the O1 El Tor biotype.
Haiti's 2010 cholera outbreak — triggered after the earthquake — killed over 10,000 people and infected nearly 1 million.
Cholera is entirely preventable through access to safe water and sanitation — it is fundamentally a disease of poverty.

faq.a: The primary treatment is rapid oral rehydration with ORS (oral rehydration salts) to replace fluids and electrolytes lost through diarrhoea. Severe cases require intravenous fluids and antibiotics (doxycycline or azithromycin). With proper treatment, the case fatality rate drops to below 1%.

Yes. WHO prequalifies two oral cholera vaccines (OCVs): Shanchol and Euvichol-Plus. Both are two-dose vaccines providing 65–85% protection for 2–3 years. In 2023, a record 36 million doses were deployed globally in outbreak response.

faq.q: Why is cholera resurging globally in 2026?
faq.a: The resurgence is driven by a convergence of factors: ongoing conflicts destroying water infrastructure, climate change increasing flooding, COVID-19 disruption of routine health services, and a global shortage of oral cholera vaccine doses relative to demand.
